children: were struggling to remain positive in after-hours trading after the company reported mixed results for the third quarter and raised their profit guidance for the year but delivered soft direct-to-consumer sales that fell short of the company’s expectations.

The company also lowered its net revenue guidance for the year, now expecting sales to be up 7% versus an earlier projection of 7% to 7.5% growth. Organic net sales are seen rising 6% compared to an earlier estimate of 5.5% to 6%.

“We saw strong growth in our international and wholesale businesses and continued momentum across our lifestyle categories,” said Levi Strauss CEO Michelle Gass. “While our direct-to-consumer business fell short of our internal expectations, we moved quickly to address the shortfall and are encouraged by the strength we are seeing heading into the holiday season, including in the U.S. Based on the acceleration in recent trends, our DTC business is on track to deliver mid-single-digit growth in the fourth quarter.”

With the benefit of IEEPA tariff refunds, Levi’s earned an adjusted profit of $0.48 per share, up 41% year-over-year and $0.12 better than expected. Tariff refunds contributed $0.16, of which $0.05 was redeployed into the business. The tariff refund benefit, net of redeployment, was $0.11.
The company demonstrated solid sales growth across regions, resulting in overall sales of $1.6B, up 4% from the same quarter last year but $10M short of expectations.

DTC sales also showed a modest increase thanks to gains in the Americas and an 8% increase in Asia. But DTC sales in the U.S. were down 1% and down 2% in Europe. Comparable sales in the company’s DTC channel—which comprised 45% of total net revenue during the third quarter—were unchanged year-over-year.

The tariff refund also boosted margins, with operating margin expanding to 13.8% from 10.8% a year ago and gross margin rising to 66.2% from 61.7%, including a 490-basis-point benefit from the refund.
Looking ahead to the remainder of 2026 and reflecting $35M of IEEPA tariff refunds in the fourth quarter, Levi Strauss
now expects to earn a profit within a range of $1.54 and $1.56 per share from $1.46 and $1.52 per share, initially, versus estimates for a profit of $1.54 per share.

The company also expects gross margin to expand by 130 basis points compared to an earlier outlook for 10 basis points of expansion and adjusted EBIT margin to expand 70 basis points to 12.1% versus earlier guidance for 60 basis points of expansion to 12%.
This guidance assumes no significant worsening of macroeconomic pressures, inflationary pressures, supply chain disruptions, potential tariffs, or currency fluctuations.

title: Levi Strauss raises FY26 profit guidance but trims sales growth outlook
